key_points.point: The author's long career starting in 1984 suggests a perspective that views current AI developments as part of a long-term, incremental evolution of software engineering. Skeptics would align with this view, arguing that AI is not a revolutionary force but rather a tool that is being integrated into existing, well-established work practices. This perspective resists the hype surrounding AI by grounding it in the reality of decades of software development experience.

The title 'Practical Tech Leader' suggests an intention to demystify AI by focusing on its practical, day-to-day application in software engineering. Skeptics would support this approach, as it strips away the anthropomorphic and revolutionary rhetoric often used to describe AI. By treating AI as a tool for a 'practical' leader, the document frames it as standard, fallible enterprise software.

The document's requirement for JavaScript to function correctly serves as a reminder of the fragility and complexity of modern software systems. Skeptics would point to this as evidence that even basic web functionality is subject to technical limitations and dependencies. This highlights the 'jagged' nature of technological progress, where new capabilities often introduce new points of failure and complexity.
